title: Acellular Life — Chapter Test
notes: Transcribed and condensed explanations; Q12 AIDS definition corrected and Q13 latency description scientifically qualified.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Based on nucleic acid type, viruses can be classified as:
questions.explanation: Nucleic acid type separates DNA and RNA viruses; strand number and envelope are separate classifications.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A virus with icosahedral (polyhedral) symmetry is:
questions.explanation: Adenovirus has an icosahedral capsid; TMV and rabies viruses are helical.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a double-stranded DNA virus?
questions.explanation: Herpesviruses carry double-stranded DNA, unlike the RNA viruses listed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: On the basis of the presence or absence of an outer lipid layer, viruses are classified as:
questions.explanation: The lipid envelope distinguishes enveloped from naked viruses.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which virus classification criterion considers the number of nucleic acid strands?
questions.explanation: Strand number defines single- versus double-stranded genomes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hepatitis B virus contains:
questions.explanation: HBV has a partially double-stranded DNA genome and uses reverse transcriptase.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The lytic cycle of a bacteriophage ends with:
options: Lysis of host cell releasing new virions
questions.explanation: The host cell bursts and releases newly formed phages at the end of the lytic cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is NOT a criterion used for virus classification?
questions.explanation: Viruses are not classified by chlorophyll because they do not photosynthesize.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: HIV belongs to which virus family?
questions.explanation: HIV is a retrovirus in the family Retroviridae.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which is NOT a common mode of HIV transmission?
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes do not transmit HIV; the other listed routes can transmit infection.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: HIV can be transmitted through all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Ordinary handshakes do not exchange the body fluids needed to transmit HIV.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An HIV-infected person is diagnosed with AIDS when:
options: CD4+ T-cell count is critically low and/or an AIDS-defining illness occurs
questions.explanation: AIDS is diagnosed at a CD4 count below 200 cells/mm³ or with an AIDS-defining illness; both are not required.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The clinical latency stage of HIV infection is characterized by:
options: Persistent infection with few or no symptoms
questions.explanation: HIV persists and continues replicating during clinical latency, often with few symptoms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A hallmark of progression to AIDS is:
options: Opportunistic infections due to weakened immunity
questions.explanation: Loss of immune function permits infections that healthy immunity usually controls.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which practice reduces the risk of HIV transmission?
questions.explanation: Condoms and sterile injection equipment reduce routes of HIV transmission.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which HIV vaccine is approved for widespread global clinical use?
options: No fully approved HIV vaccine exists
questions.explanation: No licensed HIV vaccine is currently available for routine widespread use; the other vaccines target different diseases.
